title: How to Make a Drop-Down List in Google Sheets
dek: To make a drop-down list in Google Sheets, select the cells, open Data > Data validation, add a rule with the Dropdown criteria, and enter your options. Here is how to build, edit, and troubleshoot one.

seo.metaTitle: How to Make a Drop-Down List in Google Sheets
seo.metaDescription: Make a drop-down list in Google Sheets with Data validation: add a Dropdown rule and enter your options — plus how to edit and fix common issues.

sources.label: Google Docs Editors Help — Create a dropdown list

richText: Drop-down lists keep a sheet tidy by letting people pick from set options instead of typing (and mistyping) values. In Google Sheets they take about a minute to set up, and you can build one from a typed list or from a range of cells.

body.text: How to make a drop-down list

items: Select the cell or cells where you want the drop-down.
Type each option and press Enter to add the next one. You can give each a color if you like.
Click Done. Each cell now shows a chip you can click to pick an option.

body.richText: A faster route: select the cells and use the Insert menu > Dropdown. It opens the same panel with the Dropdown criteria already chosen.

body.text: Use a list from a range (easier to update)

body.text: Edit or remove a drop-down list

items: To change the options: click the cell, then the chip's menu (or reopen Data > Data validation) and edit the rule.

To reuse it: copy the cell and Paste special > Data validation only onto other cells.

items.question: How do I add color to a drop-down list in Google Sheets?
items.answerRichText: When you add or edit the Dropdown options in Data validation, each option has a color picker next to it. Pick a color and the cell fills with it whenever that option is selected.

items.question: Can I make a dependent (conditional) drop-down list in Google Sheets?
items.answerRichText: Yes. A dependent list changes its options based on another cell — for example, choosing a country then showing only its cities. It uses helper ranges and formulas like INDIRECT or FILTER, and is a step up from a basic list.

items.question: Why won't my Google Sheets drop-down let me type other values?
items.answerRichText: The rule is set to reject anything outside the list. Open Data > Data validation, and under "If the data is invalid" switch from Reject the input to Show a warning, which allows other entries.
